I re-fetched every URL myself on 2026-09-16 with -A "Mokaair-editorial".

1) https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/02/2026-04089/implementing-the-guiding-and-establishing-national-innovation-for-us-stablecoins-act-for-the (researcher's source #1) — NOT REACHABLE. HTTP/2 302 with `location: https://unblock.federalregister.gov`; following redirects gives HTTP 200 but the body is `<title>Federal Register :: Request Access</title>` (10,596-byte anti-bot challenge). With a Chrome UA the same URL returns HTTP 500. The URL is genuine (it is the API's own html_url field, not a guess) but it was never actually read, yet it is listed in `sources` with checked_on 2026-09-16 and the sourcing_notes never mention this block.

2) https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/03/02/2026-04089.txt — HTTP 200, 800,323 bytes, real document ("[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 40 (Monday, March 2, 2026)] [Proposed Rules] [Pages 10202-10303] ... [FR Doc No: 2026-04089]"). Good.

3) https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-04089.json — HTTP 200, 6,982 bytes, real metadata. Good.

4) https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title12-section5901&num=0&edition=prelim — HTTP 200, 170,586 bytes, `<title>12 USC 5901: Definitions</title>`, "Text contains those laws in effect on September 15, 2026", carries a "Delayed Effective Date of Section" banner. Good.

5) FR API searches I re-ran independently: conditions[regulation_id_number]=1557-AF41 → HTTP 200, count 1; conditions[docket_id]=OCC-2025-0372 → HTTP 200, count 1. Both return only the 2026-03-02 proposed rule.

Blocks I re-tested: www.regulations.gov/docket/OCC-2025-0372 → HTTP 403 (confirmed). www.govinfo.gov PDF → HTTP 200, 695,807 bytes (reachable; correctly not cited as read). occ.gov → the researcher's description is WRONG in a dangerous way: https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-125.html returns HTTP 200, 60,104 bytes, final URL unchanged — but the body is the OCC home page, not the release. RSS, the 2026 release index and bulletin paths return HTTP 200 with the same 80,806-byte home page after rewriting to https://www.occ.treas.gov/. Only /static/ paths produced an actual redirect loop. The researcher's conclusion (no OCC release readable here) is right; its recorded block note ("302 Security Redirect for every path") would mislead a later agent that checks only status codes.

refuted.fact: Fact 15, second half: 'the parallel prohibition for foreign issuers takes effect on the GENIUS Act's effective date (12 U.S.C. 5902(b)(2))'
refuted.why: 12 U.S.C. 5902(b)(2) is not a prohibition on foreign issuers. FR footnote 12: 'The prohibition against digital asset service providers offering or selling payment stablecoins that are not issued by foreign payment stablecoin issuers that meet certain requirements goes into effect as of the effective date of the GENIUS Act. See 12 U.S.C. 5902(b)(2).' The preamble agrees: the Act 'prohibits digital asset service providers from offering or selling a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States unless the issuer is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer or the issuer is a foreign payment stablecoin issuer that meets certain requirements.' BOTH limbs of 5902(b) bind digital asset service providers; only the dates differ (b)(1) July 18, 2028, (b)(2) the Act's effective date. As recorded it would tell readers foreign issuance itself becomes unlawful on the effective date.

refuted.fact: Fact 94, second sentence: 'This 24 does not match the 29 respondents used in most rows of the Paperwork Reduction Act burden tables in the same document.'
refuted.why: The document explains the gap; there is no unexplained inconsistency. Under 'Affected Parties': 'a total of 29 entities ... 12 OCC-regulated national banks and Federal savings associations will have permitted payment stablecoin issuer affiliated subsidiaries ... at least 12 currently non-OCC regulated institutions ... The OCC estimates that there will be five white-label or consortia issuers'. 12+12+5 = 29. The 12+12 is a narrower cost-of-equity-capital assumption. The sentence is the researcher's own inference stated as a fact, and is additionally mis-flagged is_vendor_claim: true (a regulator's analytic assumption is not a vendor claim).

refuted.fact: Fact 84, first clause: 'it must make efforts to cure by the end of the following quarter'
refuted.why: No such duty or deadline exists in proposed Sec. 15.41(c) or its preamble. 15.41(c)(2): the issuer 'is prohibited from issuing any new payment stablecoins ... starting on the first day of the following month and until such time as it satisfies its minimum capital and backstop requirements.' 15.41(c)(3) sets the two-consecutive-quarter liquidation trigger. The only cure wording anywhere is 'remediated the shortfall' in the separate Sec. 15.11(g)(2) reserve provision. The rest of fact 84 is supported (the 'at the start of the following month' liquidation timing is in the preamble).

refuted.fact: sourcing_notes: 'www.occ.gov and www.occ.treas.gov return HTTP/1.1 302 Security Redirect ... for every path tried'
refuted.why: Not the behaviour today. The exact release the rule cites, https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-125.html, returns HTTP 200, 60,104 bytes, final URL unchanged, serving the OCC home page instead of the release. Other paths return HTTP 200 with an 80,806-byte home page after rewriting to www.occ.treas.gov. The exclusion decision is right and I reached it independently, but this block note is going into the batch-4 notes and would let a later agent record a 200 home page as a news release.

unsupported.fact: Facts 1, 2 and 5: verbatim_quote strings 'AGENCY: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Treasury.', '[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 40 (Monday, March 2, 2026)] [Proposed Rules] [Pages 10202-10303]' and 'DATES: Comments must be received by May 1, 2026.' are attached to the API JSON URL
unsupported.why: None of those three strings is in the JSON; they are in the full-text document. The JSON carries the same information in structured fields ('action', 'agencies', 'citation', 'volume', 'start_page', 'end_page', 'page_length', 'dates' without the 'DATES:' prefix, 'comments_close_on'). Every underlying fact is true and I confirmed each in both places — only the quote-to-URL mapping is wrong, which the BRIEF's one-fact-one-fetched-url rule forbids. Re-point the quotes to the .txt URL.

unsupported.fact: Fact 11: the docket's supporting documents (Coinbase 2026-06-24 / OCC-2025-0372-0355, Circle 2026-05-22 / OCC-2025-0372-0350) recorded with is_vendor_claim: false and no provenance caveat
unsupported.why: Both entries are present and I re-read them today, but they come from the same regulations_dot_gov_info cache block as fact 10, which the researcher itself flagged as the Federal Register's reading of Regulations.gov as of 2026-07-30T22:55:04Z and unverifiable at source (regulations.gov is 403 here). Flagging fact 10 and not fact 11 is inconsistent. The API also returns only the 10 most recent of 26 supporting documents, so the list read is partial.

unsupported.fact: Fact 16: the proposed definition of 'payment stablecoin'
unsupported.why: Correct and it is indeed the proposed rule's own definition, but it drops an operative carve-out: the issuer must be obligated to convert, redeem or repurchase 'for a fixed amount of monetary value, NOT INCLUDING a digital asset denominated in a fixed amount of monetary value.' That clause is what keeps stablecoin-for-stablecoin redemption outside the definition.

unsupported.fact: Fact 87: the 35 percent (up to 55 percent) reduction attributed only to proposed Sec. 8.10
unsupported.why: Incomplete. The document proposes the same baseline 35 percent (up to 55 percent) reduction in two places — for national banks and Federal savings associations under the revised Sec. 8.2, and for subpart B institutions under proposed Sec. 8.10. Recording it only under 8.10 would make an article say bank issuers get no discount.

unsupported.fact: Fact 89: 'a minimum fee associated with the first $1 billion of custodial assets'
unsupported.why: The rule does not tie the minimum fee to 'the first $1 billion'. Proposed Sec. 8.11(a)(1) is a flat minimum fee whose amount is set in the annual Notice of Fees; (a)(2) is 'Additional amount for certain assets in excess of $1 billion'. Also the reg text threshold is '50 percent or more of their INTEREST AND NON-INTEREST income', not just 'income'.

unsupported.fact: Fact 73: 'crosses $10 billion in outstanding issuance value'
unsupported.why: The statutory and regulatory trigger (proposed Sec. 15.15(b), 12 U.S.C. 5903(d)) is an outstanding issuance value of MORE THAN $10 billion. At exactly $10 billion nothing is triggered.

unsupported.fact: Fact 61: exam-cycle condition '(2) no person acquired control during the preceding 12-month period'
unsupported.why: The condition is narrower: 'No person acquired control ... during the preceding 12-month period IN WHICH A FULL-SCOPE EXAMINATION WOULD HAVE BEEN REQUIRED BUT FOR this paragraph (d).' Dropping the qualifier changes which period is measured.

unsupported.fact: Fact 97: '$11.9 million in assessment fees in 2026' — supported, flagged only as a trap
unsupported.why: The OCC does write 'a total of $11.9 million in assessment fee costs in 2026', so the fact stands. But the Total Impact paragraph of the same document renders the identical figure as '$11,929,204 million', a typo in the Federal Register text. Note it so no later editor 'corrects' the figure upward or quotes the garbled string.

additional_findings: MISSING, material — the amendment to 12 CFR 3.22 (new paragraph (i)) is the entire reason part 3 is in the title, and the pack records only that part 3 is amended. An insured national bank or Federal savings association consolidated with a permitted payment stablecoin issuer would have to (1) deconsolidate the issuer from its balance sheet, (2) deduct from common equity tier 1 capital any positive retained earnings originating from the issuer to the extent not paid out as dividends to the bank, and (3) exclude any investment in and receivable from the issuer when calculating standardized and advanced-approaches risk-weighted assets, average total consolidated assets and total leverage exposure. Sec. 6.2 gets the conforming prompt-corrective-action change. Source: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/03/02/2026-04089.txt

MISSING, material and squarely on the article's redemption angle — proposed Sec. 15.16 'Unusual and exigent circumstances' (implementing GENIUS Act section 7, 12 U.S.C. 5906). If the OCC finds unusual and exigent circumstances and reasonable cause to believe a nonbank State qualified payment stablecoin issuer's continued activity (including failure to act) is a serious risk to its financial safety, soundness or stability, the OCC 'will impose such restrictions as the OCC determines to be necessary ... in the form of a directive with the effect of a cease-and-desist order that has become final', and the listed restrictions expressly include 'Limitations on: (1) Redemptions of payment stablecoins'. The pack names Sec. 15.16 once, only as a scope cross-reference in fact 18, and never says what it does. Describing the two-business-day redemption right without it is incomplete.

MISSING — proposed Sec. 15.42 'Individual additional capital or backstop requirement': the OCC may impose additional capital or backstop on an individual issuer, with seven listed example circumstances including 'significant volatility in stablecoin issuance or redemption' and adverse effects from affiliates. This materially qualifies fact 80's 'does not propose ... a minimum amount of any single element'.

MISSING — proposed Sec. 15.41(d): an uninsured national trust bank, whether or not it is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, may ELECT to comply with the Sec. 15.41 minimum capital and backstop requirements in lieu of the minimum capital and leverage requirements in 12 CFR part 3; the election takes effect 30 days after OCC receipt unless the OCC objects in writing for good cause.
MISSING — proposed Sec. 8.12, fees for special examinations and investigations of institutions newly covered under subpart B. Fact 86 implies only 8.10 and 8.11 are new.

DATE CONFLICT to keep straight — the same API JSON gives comments_close_on 2026-05-01 (matching the DATES line 'Comments must be received by May 1, 2026') while the embedded Regulations.gov docket record inside it gives comment_end_date 2026-05-02. Use 2026-05-01.

BETTER FIRST-PARTY SUPPORT for the pack's central 'not in force' point — the uscode.house.gov page for 12 U.S.C. 5901 carries a 'Delayed Effective Date of Section' banner above the source credit and states 'Text contains those laws in effect on September 15, 2026'. That is first-party confirmation that the codified GENIUS Act text was still not in force the day before the check date, stronger than reciting the two-branch formula alone.

The document is internally inconsistent about the new part's heading: the amendatory instruction reads 'Add part 15 to read as follows: PART 15--PAYMENT STABLECOINS' while the authority-citation listing reads 'PART 15--STABLECOIN'. If the article names the heading, use the amendatory instruction's version.
